newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: G10 central banks not planning gold sales.
newsitem.headline: G10 central banks not planning gold sales.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said the group of 10 central banks had "no intention" for the time being to sell any gold.
Speaking as chairman of the G10 central bank governors committee, Tietmeyer also told reporters that the Dutch central bank had, or would be publishing a statement about its recent gold sales.

The Dutch central bank said on Monday it had sold 300 tonnes of gold "in the past period" for about 6.4 billion guilders. The Dutch government said sale of the gold from the country's central bank reserves would boost government revenues by 250 million guilders a year.
The Dutch central bank said the income from the sale, would be invested in bonds denominated in dollars, German marks and Japanese yen.
"For the time being, there is no intention for central banks to sell gold," Tietmeyer said.
Asked whether Tietmeyer's statement on gold sales refered to G10 countries, Tietmeyer said, "yes."
Tietmeyer noted there was no "formal agreement" about gold sales, but did say that those attending the meeting indicated they had no such intentions.
